conclusion.label: hedged

report:
# Does Hypnosis Help with Smoking Cessation?

**Conclusion: The evidence is inconclusive.** Despite hypnotherapy's popularity as a quit-smoking method, high-quality systematic reviews have not established that it is more effective than other cessation approaches or no treatment at all.

The most authoritative source on this question is the **Cochrane Review** on hypnotherapy for smoking cessation, widely regarded as the gold standard for evidence synthesis. The Cochrane review found **insufficient evidence** to determine whether hypnotherapy helps people quit smoking more effectively than other methods, largely due to a high risk of bias in the included studies and substantial heterogeneity across trial designs (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20927723/, https://www.cochranelibrary.com/cdsr/doi/10.1002/14651858.CD004407.pub4/full).

A 2023 meta-analytic overview published in *Frontiers in Psychology* examined multiple reviews—including three Cochrane reviews—comparing hypnosis to control conditions for smoking cessation. Of six reported effect sizes (ranging from d = 0.12 to d = 0.84), only two were statistically significant, reinforcing the picture of weak and inconsistent evidence (https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2023.1330238/full).

A separate 2024 *Frontiers* review comparing hypnotherapy to cognitive-behavioral therapy concluded that hypnotherapy's efficacy as a tobacco cessation intervention "cannot be considered sufficiently proven due to significant methodological limitations" in the available studies (https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2024.1330362/full).

More recent, broader reviews (e.g., Ekanayake and Elkins, 2025, cited secondarily) have reported more favorable results, but these take a less rigorous methodological approach than Cochrane standards and should be interpreted cautiously (https://www.ishhypnosis.org/encyclopedia/the-potential-benefit-of-hypnosis-for-smoking-cessation/).

**Bottom line:** While some studies suggest potential benefit, methodologically rigorous evidence (Cochrane) does not confirm hypnosis is an effective, reliable stand-alone smoking cessation method. It may be reasonable as a complementary approach, but shouldn't replace treatments with stronger evidence (e.g., nicotine replacement therapy, medications).
